symptom: No way to change a brain entry's wording: every correction was drop + capture, which minted a new id and orphaned the old handle; editing the id-stable way exposed that duplicate detection compared stored ids, so the edited wording re-captured was accepted twice and the original wording collided with the edited entry's handle ('already carries entry 66dcf4' quoting text that no longer says that)
cause: `Queue.Append` and `Store.Promote` deduplicated on `existing.ID == e.ID`, which is only a content check while an id still matches its text; resolve and rename already broke that, edit breaks it routinely
insight: **Once an id is a handle, identity and content are two keys, and every comparison has to say which one it means.** Duplicate = same ContentKey; collision = same id with different content, solved by deriving a fresh id (content + counter) at capture rather than refusing a legitimate new fact. Routing is the other trap: a decision follows its anchors only if it was where its anchors put it, or an entry pinned to project.md is evicted by an edit. Stubbing AssignFreeID reproduces the exact predicted error through the CLI. Harness gotcha found on the way: cobra StringSlice flags APPEND across runs of the shared rootCmd, so a second `capture -a X` in one test captured [X, X] and silently became a different entry — reset every flag to DefValue, and Changed, between runs
